postmortem.what_happened: J053 held a one-point lean to a lower US 10-year yield for three marks: the yield fell about 6bp to 4.85% on 25 Nov in the AI-led equity unwind, then rose about 9bp on 27 Nov in thin post-Thanksgiving trade as the haven bid faded. The CLI closed it at 4.94% when the 26 Nov forecast moved to 49% and flipped the side.
postmortem.assessment: A 51% forecast held for three days is noise, not a test of the thesis that falling oil would pull long yields down; the result (-0.02% net, mostly costs) says nothing about skill. The process weakness is that a one-point lean flipped to the other one-point lean after two days, paying round-trip costs on a forecast that never moved meaningfully from even. The underlying driver that mattered, a risk-off haven bid and its reversal, was not in the thesis.
postmortem.do_differently: Treat a 1-point move across 50 as a costly change and require new evidence, not a reweighting of the same news, before flipping; name the equity-risk channel explicitly in US10Y reasoning when tech volatility is high; prefer holding the prior side when the evidence is genuinely balanced.
